result:
Solution 1 looks most likely correct, but I am working from partial recall of the literature and have not proved its classification.

- **Solution 2** gives {1/3, 2/5, 1/2}. That is the set of chromatic thresholds (the minimum degree forcing bounded chromatic number), not the thresholds for being 2-colourable. So it answers a different question.
- **Solution 3** claims the values 2/(2k+3) are all attained, which would make the sum infinite. This misses that for H with large odd girth, a non-bipartite H-free graph can contain a triangle. Take a triangle with a balanced complete bipartite graph attached to each vertex. This graph is non-bipartite and has minimum degree about n/6. It is H-free when the odd girth of H is at least 5 and H has an edge meeting every odd cycle. So the thresholds cannot drop below 1/6, and the set is not infinite. Solution 3 also mishandles the case where H has no edge meeting all odd cycles.
- **Solution 1** accounts for this triangle construction. It also gets the thresholds for small odd girth from blow-ups of odd cycles, 2/5, 2/7, 2/9 and 2/11, and 1/2 when no single edge meets all odd cycles. This gives a finite set whose sum is 6086/3465. I did not verify its claimed upper bounds, such as the exact value for odd girth 5.

CHOICE: 1
